newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to host thinking conference.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to host thinking conference.

text.p: Singapore will host an international conference on thinking next month, officials said on Thursday.
Leo Tan, director of Singapore's National Institute of Education (NIE), told reporters the conference was part of the city-state's drive to promote creativity in education.
Edward de Bono, who pioneered the concept of lateral thinking, would be among 20 speakers discussing the theory and teaching of diferent ways of thinking, he said.
"This is all part of a new five-year plan of the government for education which sees creativity and thinking as the priority," he said.
The government has committed Singapore $2.5 billion (US$1.77 billion) to a plan to introduce innovative thinking into classrooms and improving the handling of information technology.

It aims to get students to think for themselves and overcome what sociologists say are cultural inhibitions among some Asian communities that tend to discourage independent thinking, the questioning of authority and of established assumptions.
Employers have complained that Singaporeans are better copiers than creators, and sometimes need too much hand-holding when introduced to new tasks or challenges.

Tan said the Singapore conference, the seventh in a series of international discussions on thinking and the first in Southeast Asia, would focus on the practical benefits of creative thinking for business and the community. The June 1-6 meeting will gather330 delegates from 34 countries.
"For the first time, there will be less concentration on academics. More than 1,000 school principals and teachers will attend," he said.
